cells.tense: The exchange is happening here, and both sides are receiving what they gave
cells.ask: Take one arrangement in your shared life that already runs both ways and hold its shape — who brings what, how it splits — set once where both can see it, then walk on
cells.core:
You are standing somewhere people keep what has proven worth keeping — the words, habits and ways passed on because they work. And you can take from that place, not only feed it. What returns to you is real and you count it correctly, no quiet deficit running behind the scenes. You handle the exchange well, and it sits level because you handle it.

Now let the level persist for a stretch. Take one arrangement in this place that already runs both ways and give its terms a form that lasts — who brings what, how it is split, stated once. Then the days you are absent, it stays even without your eye on it. The same steadiness you give everything here, you are now turning toward your own receiving.

cells.tense: You are guarding the fairness ahead of the moment, before anyone has asked
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: For seven days, give what you give and stop scanning for who is short — no tallying, no count of what comes back — just carry the week's work on yourself
cells.core:
In the shared meanings you move through, you are holding the scales before they need holding. You see a debt forming before it lands, you tilt things back before anyone feels the tilt, and the room cannot breathe without your eye on the balance. It reads as care. From the other side it feels like being weighed.

Fairness has a looser face. For a week, keep going on your own reserves and stop checking on anyone else. Give what you give, count nothing, and let what returns arrive without your watching for it. If something is truly off by the week's close, you will notice it without having hunted it. The work is holding what you care about without closing your hand around it, and finding it holds anyway.

cells.tense: The exchange was running, and you are at a door that already closed behind you
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Write one line on paper separating what carries weight in an exchange from what does not — cross off one item on the wrong side and leave the page as it is
cells.core:
Here, in the place where meaning gets handed on, the exchange runs one direction. You pour in — attention, hours, the work of keeping things going — and little comes back. Things offered to you arrive and do not land. You are holding what the exchange was when it was even, not looking at what it is now.

Look closer. Pick one arrangement and draw a line between the part that matters and the part that does not — a single distinction, written down, visible. Cross off one thing that does not serve. That is the act. Telling things apart is what sharpens the hand again, and this hand wants the sharpening before you ask anyone for anything. The exchange moves back toward even through your own eye first, not through someone else's answer.

cells.tense: You are already the one settling fairness in this place, and the pen is down
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Next time you move to even something out in your shared life, wait a beat first — know it is you making the adjustment — and then adjust it or pass
cells.core:
You are the one doing the fairness in this place. When something in the shared meaning needs evening out, your hand moves — an adjustment, a nudge to who gets what, the thing kept level. Ask you and you would say the group finds its own way. That hand belongs to you, and you do not see it as yours.

The gap between a bystander and the one keeping this place is that the keeper knows. So slow down before the next quiet adjustment. Hold both truths at once — that things could run without you, and that you are about to move — sit with them, then move or do not. Either is allowed. Nothing hangs on which you pick. What changes is your name on the act, and that has been missing.

If I am wrong about the scale of the overcaring, the ask survives because it still returns something to the person regardless. The Too Much cell must not shame the deep care; it names what happens when holding for others becomes holding against the moment. The Unacknowledged cell must not flatter; it notes only that the authorship has slipped, not that the person is secretly wise.
